title: Giving Up a Mountain Dining Plans Plan and the Return of a Balance
content:
A household may give a plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range up. The plan's refund basis decides what comes back: on the loaded amount basis the balance is returned less every bonus still unspent, on the full balance basis the whole balance is returned, and on the no refund basis nothing is returned and the balance must be spent before the season ends. A balance is returned only while the plan record stands in the active, suspended, exhausted, cancelled or expired state. A refund is asked for no later than the plan's refund window counted in calendar days from the day the plan was opened. Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used. The plan's administration fee is retained from whatever is returned, and the money goes back to the method it was loaded from rather than to any other. Where the collective's own error caused the cancellation, nothing is retained and the bonus is returned with the balance.

## The three bases

| The plan's refund basis | What is returned, before the administration fee |
| --- | --- |
| loaded amount less bonus | the balance standing on the plan, less every bonus still unspent |
| full balance | the whole balance standing on the plan |
| no refund | nothing at all; the balance is to be spent before the season ends |

From whatever is returned the plan's administration fee is retained, and what remains goes back to the method the money was loaded from and to no other method.

Where the cancellation was caused by the collective's own error the terms differ in two respects: nothing is retained, and the bonus is returned together with the balance.

## A worked return, on hypothetical figures

A plan stands on the loaded amount less bonus basis and carries an administration fee of $35.00. The balance is $420.00, of which $60.00 is bonus still unspent. What the basis returns is the balance less the unspent bonus, which is $360.00. The administration fee is retained from that figure, so $325.00 goes back, and it goes back to the method the money was loaded from.

Had the same cancellation been caused by the collective's own error, nothing would have been retained and the unspent bonus would have gone back with the balance, so the whole $420.00 would have been returned.

## The state, and the window

A balance goes back only while the plan record stands in one of five states: active, suspended, exhausted, cancelled or expired. The state is read from the collective's own record of the plan.

The refund window runs in calendar days from the day the plan was opened, that day counting as day zero, and the last day of the window counts as within it. **A boundary reading on hypothetical figures:** a plan carrying a refund window of 45 calendar days is opened on 2026-12-01; day 45 is 2027-01-15. A refund asked for on 2027-01-15 is asked for no later than the window allows. One asked for on 2027-01-16 is not.
